description: Low-profile mechanical switch MX stem
notes: Binary. Plate cutout must be measured. Soldered. Thumb keys may want a lighter spring - decide at M1. 12.2mm tall, 1.70mm pretravel, 3.00mm total travel, 3-pin. Datasheet and STEP model published by Gateron - use them, do not caliper the housing. 18 keys + 3 spares (octave up/down, hold/preset) - cutouts required in the DXF at M3 even if fitted later (ADR 0010)

description: Keycap 16.5x16.5mm blank black MX stem
notes: Sold in 5-packs - 21 keys needs 5 packs. Smaller than MX keycap spacing

description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 16 GPIO broken out (1-7, 34-40, 43, 44) vs 14 needed. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM: confirm quad at E1, octal would eat GPIO33-37. The 8x8 matrix faces out through a tail window as a second display (ADR 0014) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Pressure transducer 0-6kPa, conditioned, dual port
package: case 1351-01, dual side ports, THT leads
notes: ~1ms response = ~159Hz corner. Loop runs 4kHz; rate lives on the DAC side. DP not GP: identical transfer function (766mV/kPa, 0.2-4.7V) but IN PRODUCTION to 2028 where the GP is obsolete. Reference port left open to the cavity - it is the other face of the same diaphragm, not an outlet. Must NEVER be blocked: mask before coating. Confirm which port is P1 before layout

description: 12-bit 2-ch SAR ADC SPI
notes: SOIC-8. VDD-referenced so no separate ref chip. 50ksps at 3V3 vs 4-8kHz needed. One spare channel

description: 6-axis IMU - accel + gyro no fusion
notes: Fusion not wanted - raw accel is the signal and capture-on-press makes drift irrelevant. 6-axis confirmed from CircuitPython/Zephyr board definitions, not the listing. SDA=GPIO11 SCL=GPIO12 INT1=GPIO10 INT2=GPIO13. This IS the final IMU - the carrier is passive

description: 8-bit parallel-in shift register
notes: SOIC-16. The 'better drive over a 14in chain' rationale was backwards - faster edges into an unterminated loom ring. Kept for its native 3V3 spec, WITH 33-68R series termination. 74HC165 is a drop-in on the same footprint if E4 says otherwise

description: 1.91in 536x240 AMOLED RM67162 QSPI + ESP32-S3
notes: 60x25.5x10mm - mounts lengthwise. 18 GPIO broken out

description: 12V to 5V switching regulator module
notes: 3-pin SIP on a 7805 footprint. No inductor no feedback network no layout risk. ONE PER DEV BOARD (ADR 0013): splitting the rail keeps the display board's WiFi bursts off the real-time board and off the matrix, and 1A each clears the 928mA clamp-legal worst case that 1A shared does not

description: Addressable LED strip - one 1m reel cut into two 420mm side runs
notes: Qty is a REEL, not a length. 0.84m used of 1m. 12V native so no 5V rail. TWO independent data lines, no crossover wire. Backup data line survives a dead LED. 60/m settled on appearance; M6 can downgrade on looks

part: DAC8568C (or A grade) - full orderable P/N required
description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: Populate 7 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, breath ambient-zero, mod offset. A/C grade resets to ZERO scale - B/D reset to midscale and park pitch octaves up. Internal ref is DISABLED by default, enable at boot. AVDD from U-REG-DAC

description: Dual low-drift RRIO op-amp
notes: ONE op-amp part throughout the module - pitch, mod 1-4, breath scaling, and the VREFOUT follower. RRIO on +/-12V reaches ~11.9V. All 10 halves are now spent: 7 DAC-driven stages + breath gain + breath offset + VREFOUT buffer. No spare half remains

description: Superseded by U-OPA-PITCH
notes: Single part number beats saving a few dollars on a one-off. Removes a class of assembly error

part: LT5400BCMS8-x (MSOP option, ratio per pitch stage design)
description: Matched resistor network for pitch scaling
notes: One pitch stage, one network. MUST be the MS8 (MSOP) option, not the DFN - leadless is banned by the ADR 0013 package policy. Ratio suffix follows the final gain/offset topology. Ratio TRACKING is what matters, not absolute tempco: two discrete 10ppm thin films give 14.1ppm/degC of ratio drift, about 1.5 cents, against the LT5400's 0.11

description: 3.5mm mono PCB-mount jack
notes: De facto eurorack standard. Standard panel hole

part: Alpha 9mm vertical PCB mount, B50k linear
description: Panel potentiometer - breath gain and offset
notes: Linear taper - predictable for CV scaling. Gain then offset order

description: Panel power switch - drives the load switch enable, carries no load current
notes: Signal-level only now. The only power switch in the system; SW-PWR-INST is deleted (ADR 0005)

description: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed
notes: REPLACES TPS2553, which is a 2.5-6.5V USB switch with a 7V abs max - it would not survive first power-on at 12V. Suffix matters: -1 LATCHES OFF, -2 auto-retries. Set the limit at 1.0A with a programmed 50-100ms ramp. LM5069MM or LTC4210 equally valid

description: 8-conductor ruggedised connector, module panel and instrument tail
notes: 23.8mm cutout in a 40.34mm 8HP panel = 8.27mm each side. Brace to the PCB anyway (free). Instrument end mounts to an internal backing plate, not oak - and the D-series is rated 4mm MAX panel thickness, so it cannot mount through 6mm oak. Variant decided at E12/M7

description: Eurorack front panel
notes: Laser or waterjet from DXF - SAME vendor and order as the key plate. 8HP not 6HP: see ADR 0004

description: Aluminium key plate laser or waterjet cut
notes: Cutout 14.0 x 14.0mm, same as MX (docs/reference/ks33-geometry.md). THICKNESS OPEN: 2mm defeats the retention clips entirely, MX standard is 1.5mm, the reference KS-33 build uses 1.1mm. Decide with Gateron's clip dimension

description: Oak top and bottom panels
notes: Bottom panel thickness sets thumb key inset depth

description: Frosted acrylic side panels
notes: Edge-lit

description: Scopes, logic analysers, DMMs, signal generators, RF
notes: Full bench available - E9 not gated on tooling

description: 5.000V precision series reference for the breath sensor supply
notes: +-0.05%, 3ppm/degC, ~5ppm/V line reg. The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric so its supply IS its scale factor. Buffered by half of U-BUF

description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8. Runs on +12V not 5V - a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is at the rail so no clamp current, which kills the >=3.3k protection resistor requirement. SAME part as the module op-amps

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, so a POSITIVE REF subtracts the sensor's +0.2V pedestal and the unipolar DAC ch6 can do it. Downstream stage inverts. See hardware/module/breath-receive-stage.md

description: USB-C connector for the real-time carrier
notes: Dev boards carry these. Only required if a custom MCU carrier is ever built (ADR 0013)

description: USB ESD protection array
notes: Dev boards carry these. Only required if a custom MCU carrier is ever built (ADR 0013)

description: Boot and reset buttons
notes: Dev boards carry these. Only required if a custom MCU carrier is ever built (ADR 0013)

description: Local bulk capacitance at the display board
notes: Absorbs WiFi TX transients so they do not reach the rack rail

description: Breath tube from mouthpiece to sensor, plus dead-volume trap
notes: ~400mm - the sensor sits at the BOTTOM with the real-time board (ADR 0003), not at the top. 1.17ms propagation, the largest single term in the latency budget. Trap <=1mL and clearable without disassembly

description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3V3 reads high. Two spare gates. VERIFY WS2815 threshold

description: Level shifter, 3V3 SPI up to 5V for the DAC
notes: SAME part as the instrument LED shifter. Covers SCLK MOSI CS with a spare gate. Runs from bus +5V; the DAC runs from U-REG-DAC. OE gated from umbilical +12V presence - see R-OEGATE. Cited 0006 before, which never mentions a level shifter; the part, its rail, its thresholds and its OE gating are all ADR 0004

description: Eurorack power inlet
notes: Shrouded and keyed - reversed ribbon is the classic eurorack failure. Carries the +5V rail the module REQUIRES

description: Schottky reverse polarity protection
notes: ~0.3-0.4V drop. Community standard for eurorack power entry. THREE not two: the module's analog +12V and the umbilical feed must NOT share a diode - instrument current then modulates its Vf by ~80mV, which is ~20 cents of breath-correlated pitch bend and needs no ground path at all (ADR 0006)

description: Adjustable LDO set to 5.25V for the DAC AVDD
notes: Off protected +12V. ~13mA load incl. the divider, ~90mW. Decouples DAC full scale from the rack's +-5% +5V rail. TOLERANCE IS A BENCH TASK, NOT A SPEC TASK: worst case spans 0.66V against a ~0.55V window and no nominal value fits on paper, but this is one unit with a TO-92 part, two through-hole resistors and a voltmeter. E7 measures where the DAC's top codes start compressing against AVDD and selects R2 from that

description: LM317 output setting divider
notes: Vout = 1.25*(1+475/150) = 5.21V. WAS 240R/768R at 1%, whose stated '+-4% = 5.04-5.46V' ignored both the divider tolerance and I_ADJ. Smaller R2 halves the I_ADJ term to 24-48mV; 0.1% parts cost pennies in the same order. The LM317's own 1.20-1.30V reference is the dominant term and no divider fixes it - so R2 is SELECTED ON THE BENCH at E7 (this is a population of one), and the value here is the starting point. Buy a handful of neighbouring E96 values

description: LM317 ADJ bypass and output cap
notes: ADJ bypass drops output noise to ~50uV RMS. Output cap for LDO stability

description: Series bead per supply branch
notes: One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Rated >=1A - the common 0805 600R part is ~300mA and a saturated bead is a wire. The '470uF at the load' half of this row moved out: entry bulk is C-BULK-RAIL, strip bulk is C-STRIP-BULK, and this row was double-booking them

description: Series protection on each CV output
notes: Standard eurorack practice - survives shorts and output-to-output patching. On pitch it is a pure gain error the trimmer cancels; calibrate with the real load (ADR 0006)

description: HF decoupling at every module IC supply pin
notes: One per supply pin, close to the pin. 5 x OPA2197 on +/-12V = 10, INA828 = 2, DAC8568 AVDD+DVDD = 2, 74AHCT125, 74HC123, LT1641 VCC, LM317 in. Was 10, which is about half the real pin count

description: Pitch scale and offset trimmers
notes: Small trim range around a fixed precision resistor. Firmware still does multi-point INL correction

description: Decoupling, one per shift register board
notes: There was no controller-side decoupling at all. A 74x165's output edges brown out a local rail with no reservoir

description: Series termination on key-chain clock and latch at the MCU
notes: Source termination at the driving end. Chain the loom, do not star it; order it so data flows toward the clock source

description: Anti-alias cap at the MCP3202 input pin
notes: 564Hz with the divider's 6k Thevenin (10k||15k) - matches the 500Hz channel everywhere else. WAS 220nF, which is 121Hz and smears the breath band; the '~600Hz, 58dB at 496kHz' note was wrong twice over - wrong corner, and the R-78E5.0 switches at 330kHz not 496kHz. 55dB at 330kHz. C0G not X7R in a DC-accurate path

description: 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: Sensor reaches 4.7V into a 3V3 ADC. Divide AFTER the buffer, not before. >=10k upper leg: 5V-before-3V3 sequencing otherwise pushes ~2.5mA into the ADC ESD clamp on every power-up. Needs C-AA-ADC to still settle

description: Bulk at each WS2815 feed point
notes: Bulk belongs at the load. A ferrite is a wire at the WS2815's ~2kHz PWM rate

description: LC between the umbilical node and the buck input
notes: A real inductor, not a bead. This is the part the bead was wrongly credited for

description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: CS to +5V, SCLK and MOSI to ground. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault - floating CMOS oscillates and a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC

description: Series termination on MOSI at the driving end
notes: Series termination at the DRIVING end, which is the instrument, not the module - it was categorised 'module' and would have landed on the wrong PCB. Also removes the need for SYNC regeneration at the module end

description: Series resistor on each op-amp + input driven by the DAC
notes: Seven populated DAC channels, all driving op-amp inputs: pitch, mod 1-4, breath ambient-zero buffer (ch6), mod offset buffer (ch7). Was 5. Cross-checks U-OPA-PITCH qty 5: 7 DAC-driven halves + breath gain + breath offset = 9 halves = 4.5 duals. DAC on 5.25V and op-amps on +-12V do not come up together; bounds input clamp current, outside the feedback path so no accuracy cost. Plus one on the VREFOUT follower: 8 total

description: Clamp diodes at the CV jacks
notes: SILICON not Schottky. BAT54S leakage of 2uA through the 1k output resistor is 2mV = 2.4 cents of tempco-dependent pitch error

description: Helmholtz restrictor AND liquid-water barrier at the sensor port
notes: One part, two jobs: sizes the resonance above the 500Hz corner and blocks liquid. Size the orifice at E2. Trap volume <=1mL. Pressure port only - the DP's reference port is unplumbed

description: Frame watchdog: asserts DAC CLR when SPI traffic stops
notes: A stuck CV drones the rack forever and nothing notices. CLR parks pitch subsonic and mods at 0V - same state as rack power-on

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003)

description: Bonds the aluminium plate to PWR_GND
notes: PWR_GND, never AGND. Unbonded, the plate floats 1-2mm from 18 switch pins and fires spurious notes on touch. AGND would put body capacitance on the breath reference

description: Tail window for the 8x8 matrix
notes: NOT the side panels' frosted material - needs pixel definition, not blur. Thin and close to the LEDs. Prototype at M6

description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. Shielded preferred. It is a CONSUMABLE - keep spares and replace at the first intermittency

description: Mouthpiece - no bite sensor, raw tube is playable
notes: OD must let the lips vent at the corners - that is what makes circular breathing work. Bore settled at E2 by playing two or three sizes. Removable for cleaning

description: INA828 gain-set resistor
notes: G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185. Effective 2.161 after the bias/series divider -> 9.94V jack span. The panel gain knob absorbs the 0.6%

description: Common-mode bias return, one per in-amp input
notes: REPLACES R-PD-BREATH. Without these the in-amp floats when unplugged and saturates to a rail. ~60nA against a 350mA power return = 0.2ppm, so AGND's no-current rule survives

description: Module-side series protection, one per leg
notes: Matched. Gigaohm in-amp inputs make source impedance irrelevant to CMRR, so 10k is free

description: 500Hz filter AHEAD of the in-amp
notes: 531Hz differential. C_diff must be ~10x C_cm or a CM mismatch converts to DM. AHEAD of the amp, not after - a filter after it cannot stop RF rectification from a 2.4GHz radio 2m away

description: Breath output reconstruction cap
notes: ~480Hz with R-OUT-PROT. Film not X7R: DC bias coefficient moves the corner 30% at 10V. ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.

description: Sets the load switch current limit
notes: THE resistor that is the limit. 1.0A target; final value from E6's current-probe measurement, not from the estimated table

description: Series protection on the breath buffer output into the umbilical
notes: R1 in hardware/module/breath-receive-stage.md. 1k not 10k: it also isolates the OPA2197 from ~200pF of cable capacitance. NO instrument-end band-limit cap - the schematic puts the whole 500Hz filter at the receive end, AHEAD of the in-amp, because that is the only place it can stop RF rectification. ADR 0003's 'band-limit at both ends' is superseded by that page

description: Reconstruction filter cap on the pitch output
notes: 1k x 10nF = 15.9kHz, inside ADR 0006's 10-20kHz window. Fast so note changes land instantly. The C of R-OUT-PROT's RC, which had no C anywhere in the BOM. ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.

description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.

description: Difference-amp network per mod channel - Vout = 4 x (Vdac - 2.5V)
notes: 4 per channel x 4 channels. ADR 0006 contradicts itself - the topology section offers an LT5400 1:4, the calibration section says ordinary 1% discretes on channels 2-6. Taking the latter, which is also what 'the precision parts concentrate on channel 1' means. If the former is wanted this becomes 4 x LT5400 and this row is deleted

description: 74HC123 timing resistor - sets the frame timeout
notes: t = 0.45 x R x C. 1M with 220nF is ~99ms: well under a second, far above a 250us loop period. N is the whole specification of U-WATCHDOG and nothing in the BOM set it

description: 74HC123 timing capacitor
notes: Pairs with R-WDT for a ~99ms frame timeout

description: Pull-up on the DAC8568 CLR line
notes: Active-low CLR must not float while the monostable is being retriggered

description: Divider sensing umbilical +12V presence to drive the 74AHCT125 OE pins
notes: 12V x 47/147 = 3.84V, a valid AHCT high off the 5V rail; 0V when the load switch is off. Gates all four OE pins together. This is what makes 'instrument absent' a state the hardware knows about, which is load-bearing for ADR 0005's switching architecture

description: Clamp on the OE divider node to the 5V rail
notes: Bounds the divider node if the bus 5V rail is absent while +12V is present

description: ORs USB VBUS with the umbilical-derived 5V rail for bench use
notes: One diode per source into the shared 5V node. Both sources drop ~0.3V, leaving ~4.7V at the dev boards' 5V pins - fine for their onboard LDOs, and the breath sensor is no longer on this rail. Bench affordance for E5, explicitly not a standalone mode

description: Passive carrier: dev board headers, 165 chain, ADC, reference, buffers, level shifter, power entry
notes: Must carry the ~22mm cutout under the 8x8 matrix (ADR 0014) and the umbilical backing-plate mounting. Impossible to add later. Nothing on it is fast or RF - 2 layers, hand-assembled

description: Identical satellite board: one 74LVC165 + switches + decoupling
notes: One per cluster - left hand (5), left thumb (4), right hand (6), right thumb (3). Identical by design so the 14 spare chain bits are free expansion

description: DAC, scaling, jacks, power entry, load switch, watchdog
notes: Must brace the etherCON mechanically. 8HP not 6HP: the 23.8mm hole leaves 8.27mm of panel each side at 40.34mm (ADR 0004)

part: 2.54mm female header strip - machined or dual-wipe
description: Sockets for both dev boards on the carrier
notes: Cut to length: 2 strips for the ESP32-S3-Matrix, 2 for the T-Display-S3 AMOLED, 2 spare. SOCKETS not solder-down - a dead dev board in a bonded body is otherwise terminal

part: Ribbon with alternating grounds and/or twisted pair
description: Internal looms: key chain, LED power and data, UART, power
notes: A ground return per signal on the key chain is mandatory (ADR 0001). TWO SPARE CONDUCTORS in every loom - a few cents now, the instrument later. The looms are hand-built once into a stack that cannot be reopened

description: Bulk cap at the umbilical entry / buck input - the C of L-BUCK-IN's LC
notes: Completes the LC: L-BUCK-IN had an L and no C. One per buck. Also the capacitance the module load switch's inrush ramp is sized against (ADR 0005). 25V part on a 12V rail for derating

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 in, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there

description: Output capacitor on the REF5050
notes: Per the REF50xx datasheet's recommended output capacitance, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside. This is the rail that IS the breath scale factor

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004. NOT the 470uF strip capacitance - that belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK. Split out of FB-IN, which was ordering two different components on one line

description: Socket for the MPXV4006DP so the sensor is replaceable
notes: ADR 0003 calls the sensor a wear part and buys two. The spare is only reachable if the first part comes out, and the body is bonded. Case 1351-01 THT leads on 2.54mm

description: Panel power indicator
notes: Downstream of the load switch, so it indicates umbilical power actually present rather than rack power. With LT1641-1 latching off on a fault, this is the only thing that says why the instrument went dark

description: Series resistor for LED-PANEL
notes: ~4mA from +12V

part: Knob for the POT-BREATH shaft type
description: Knobs for the breath gain and offset pots
notes: Match the shaft of the POT-BREATH variant ordered - D-shaft and knurled are not interchangeable

part: KS-33 lighter variant - TBD at M1
description: Optional lighter-spring switches for the four left-thumb keys
notes: ADR 0002 leaves the spring weight to M1, decided by hand before anything is built. If taken, SW1-n drops by 4. Mixed weights cost nothing but a second line on the same order

description: Strap anchor through the full laminated stack
notes: Position settled empirically at the M8 pre-bond dry assembly, slightly above the centre of gravity, and not adjustable afterwards. Anchors to the PLATE STACK, never to oak

description: Internal backing plate for the etherCON and the U-bolt
notes: The D-series is rated 4mm MAX panel thickness so it cannot mount through 6mm oak. The oak is the face the screws pass through, not the thing they hold

description: Thumb switch plate, mounted to the inside face of the oak bottom
notes: Carries the 4 left-thumb and 3 right-thumb switches. Same 14.0 x 14.0mm cutout geometry, same vendor and same order as PLATE-TOP

description: Laminated thumb rest lip on the bottom panel
notes: A 2D part added by lamination - there is no pocketing anywhere in this design. The right thumb rests here and RT1-3 sit offset from the rest position

description: Lamination adhesive for the stack
notes: Keep it away from the breath sensor during lamination - a glue line across the reference port is the 5.2kPa failure in ADR 0003

description: Pull-up on every 74x165 key input
notes: UNRETROFITTABLE. 74x165 parallel inputs have NO internal pull-ups and there was no line for them anywhere - every key input floated, in a side channel shared with WS2815 power and 800kHz data. One per switch position including the 3 spare-switch bits, on the cluster boards

description: Series resistor between each switch and its 74x165 input
notes: With C-KEY: press is ~1us (100R x 10nF) so it stays instant, release is ~93us (10k x 10nF) which is a free hardware debounce. Also bounds injected current

description: Filter cap at each 74x165 key input
notes: A 12V LED edge at ~120V/us through ~15pF of loom coupling injects a full false level into an asymmetric debounce that fires on the FIRST closed sample - one spurious note-on at full velocity, unfiltered. This drops the coupling ~54dB

description: Divider from the buffered VREFOUT into the pitch offset trimmer
notes: Ratio set with the final pitch stage at E10. Replaces a bare divider off the +/-12V rail, which had ~0.21V/V sensitivity: 22 cents p-p of WS2815-correlated pitch FM and 12.5 cents of transposition when another module powers up. The offset now TRACKS the DAC full scale, since that is 2 x VREFOUT

description: Service header: EN, IO0, U0TXD, U0RXD, GND for each board
notes: UNRETROFITTABLE. The only opening in the instrument that exists for a failure. On the S3 the internal PHY is USB-Serial-JTAG OR USB-OTG, never both, so claiming OTG for USB MIDI deletes the DTR/RTS download path - one bad image ends a bonded instrument. Display board has no external connector at all

description: Removable cover over HDR-SERVICE on the tail underside
notes: Same laminated layer as the matrix window, beside it. Screws into the plate stack, not the oak. Goes into the M4 CAD with the window and the etherCON backing plate, and into the 1:1 paper check of the tail face

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. REPLACES U-TVS-UMB, which named SP3012-06UTG: that part is obsolete AND uDFN-14, not the SOT-23-6 the row claimed - leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy. It was un-orderable as written

description: ESD protection on the BREATH and AGND legs
notes: 12V STANDOFF, NOT 5V. BREATH's normal top of range is 4.7V against a 5V array's V_RWM - 300mV of margin on the project's DC-accurate output, with 1.5uA of leakage into a 1k output resistor. Worse, ADR 0003's buffer-on-+12V decision exists precisely so a SUSTAINED +12V fault on BREATH is harmless; a 5V clamp would turn that designed-safe case into a part that conducts until something fails

description: TVS across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: 15V standoff on a 12V rail. The power pair is the one the old 6-channel array could never have covered - six channels against eight conductors, and the six non-power ones are the natural fit

part: Same three groups, module end of the etherCON
description: ESD protection at the module end of the umbilical
notes: The BOM had protection at one end only. DELIBERATELY open, not forgotten: the module is behind four screws and this is retrofittable, where the instrument end is bonded shut. Fit at E12 if E11 gives any reason to
